subject: pcountOpen and parallel parboot to get goodness-of-fit on HPC

messages.author: f4bebbdb3c5fcabc
messages.subject: pcountOpen and parallel parboot to get goodness-of-fit on HPC
parts:
I have a pcountOpen model that takes quite a while to run, so now that I am trying to do parboot to get goodness-of-fit statistics, I am looking into parallel calculations to make sure I have results in a timely fashion.

I want to run this on our university's HPC but this is where the issue lies. The instructions from our HPC team was *not* to use "detectCores()" as it would detect all cores on the HPC, not just the ones assigned to you (or requested by you). So in other cases I have always used

library(doParallel)
no_cores <- as.numeric(Sys.getenv("SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK")) # this reads the correct number of cores the scheduler has given me
myCluster <- makeCluster(no_cores, type= "FORK")
registerDoParallel(myCluster)
# and then do whatever loop I needed to do with foreach()

However, if I understand the code correctly, the following line is hardcoded in parboot()

coresToUse <- detectCores() - 1

Is this correct? If so, is there any way to set the number of cores differently?

And another, kind of related question: "Nmix.gof.test" does something similar? Also for pcountOpen models? Can this function be run in parallel?

Thanks for any help and insights!

messages.author: 4e956cc50ac3e075
messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] pcountOpen and parallel parboot to get goodness-of-fit on HPC
parts:
Hi Geraldine,


Nmix.gof.test( ) is a wrapper for parboot( ) and uses the default values of parboot (parallel = TRUE), so yes, it behaves like parboot( ) and uses detectCores( ). I'm working on the function at the moment with some other changes and will include an additional argument to make this clear and allow to user to choose not to run it in parallel.


Best,


Marc

parts:
Hi Geraldine,

Unfortunately, there is no parallel option for nonparboot. Ian Fiske wrote this function, and I don't recall how it handles NAs. However, I believe it does return each resampled dataset, so you could always work directly with those. Or you could avoid nonparboot all together and write similar code to resample the data and then fit models to each dataset. That way, you could do things in parallel.

You are correct about the "bsType" argument.

Richard
